lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say. Then practise develops listening and speaking by modelling pronunciation and giving students the chance to practise saying the target words or phrases with the correct intonation and stress at phrase level.
Look for careful listening, speaking fluency, confident repetition and taking turns.
“I love that I can ride my bike and I can swim at the weekends. What can you do?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - B. Look and say

details: Look and say develops oral accuracy and comprehension as students describe activities using simple sentence prompts.
Look for correct answers, speaking fluency and contextually correct sentences.
“Here’s a picture I took last weekend! What can all my friends do?”

details: Look and circle develops writing accuracy and comprehension by helping students match pictures to words and circle the correct word related to that image.
Look for correct matching of pictures and words and neat circling.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - Speaking Toss a coin and say

details: Toss a coin and say helps students practice pronunciation of target vocabulary as they play the game together.
Look for taking turns, confident pronunciation and correct identification of the activities shown in the game.
“Let’s have a board game adventure! Let’;s see what our friends are doing as we move up the water hose!”
